TH SERIES
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 7 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: The TH9 is the full-size 9mm of Taurus's TH series, and the series book covers six guns at once - TH9, TH40, TH9C, TH40C, TH10 and TH45. That matters here because several of the TH9's controls are listed as full-size-only, so the compact TH9C beside it in the same table is not the same gun. The TH9 is hammer-fired, double and single action with a decocker, and its field strip is a five-step latch takedown.

steps.title: TH9, not TH9C - and not one of the other four in this book
steps.action: Confirm the model against the table: the TH9 is 9mm Luger, 17 rounds, 4.27-inch barrel, 7.72 inches overall, 5.98 high, 28.2 ounces. The TH9C in the next column is 13 rounds on a 3.54-inch barrel at 6.85 overall - a different gun sharing this book with the TH40, TH40C, TH10 and TH45.
steps.prose: One book, six pistols, and Taurus separates them only in this table and in a handful of parenthetical notes. Everything that follows is written for the full-size TH9; where the book qualifies a feature by frame size, this guide says so rather than letting the qualification pass silently.
steps.cite:
TH SERIES
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 7 — Specifications, printed p.14 (PDF p.8)

steps.title: Full-size-only controls: ambidextrous safety, decocker, slide catch, backstraps
steps.action: Check what your TH9 actually carries before you handle it as if it were another TH. Taurus lists the manual safety and the hammer decocker as ambidextrous on FULL SIZE models, and the ambidextrous slide catch as a full-size feature - the magazine release is ambidextrous on all models.
steps.prose: This is the single most important variant note in the TH book, because the decocker and safety are the same lever on this pistol: down decocks, up is safe. On a full-size TH9 that lever exists on both sides, so a left-handed shooter can reach it; on a compact it may be one side only. Establish which you have before you rely on the off-hand lever in the dark.
steps.caution: The adjustable backstrap is a full-size-only feature too: Taurus lists 'Adjustable backstrap (Full Size models only)' among the TH remarks, so a TH9C owner should not go looking for the backstrap pin.
steps.quote:
Manual Safety (Ambidextrous on Full Size models) 
Hammer Decocker (Ambidextrous on Full Size models)
steps.cite:
TH SERIES
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 7 — Specifications, printed p.14 (PDF p.8)

steps.title: Magazine out, slide back and locked, look and feel
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction and finger on the memory pad, press the magazine release and pull the magazine. Pull the slide to the rear, lock it back, then look and feel the magazine well and the chamber.
steps.prose: A 17-round TH9 magazine is long and heavy enough that people judge it loaded or empty by weight, which is exactly the habit this step exists to break. The loaded chamber indicator on the slide is a prompt only - it can be held proud by fouling on an empty chamber and lie in the other direction too.
steps.quote: 1. Before disassembly always (1) Keep your finger off or the trigger and on the memory pad, (2) point the muzzle in a safe direction (3) remove the magazine by pressing the magazine release button (4) pulling the slide to the rear and locking back and (5) looking and feeling the magazine well and chamber to confirm the pistol is empty. An empty firearm cannot fire.
steps.cite:
TH SERIES
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 7 — Disassembly, printed p.26 (PDF p.14)
steps.warn: After removing the magazine, always check the chamber and make sure it is empty.

steps.title: TH series pistols have no magazine disconnector
steps.action: Do not let the magazine leaving the gun stand in for a chamber check. Taurus states that TH series pistols have no magazine disconnector and will fire with the magazine removed.
steps.prose: On a hammer gun the risk reads differently from a striker gun's, because a decocked TH9 looks obviously safe - hammer down, lever up - and it is still a loaded pistol if a round is chambered. Decocking is not unloading, and the strip below asks you to pull the trigger.
steps.aside: Taurus's own sequence for stopping mid-magazine is to decock first by moving the safety downward, then push the lever up to the 'on' position, and only then clear the firearm.
steps.quote: Taurus TH Series pistols do not have a magazine disconnector
steps.cite:
TH SERIES
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 7 — Operating Instructions, printed p.23 (PDF p.12)

steps.title: Slide back an eighth of an inch, disassembly latch down
steps.action: Take the slide with four fingers over the top and your thumb on the rear of the grip - either hand works on a full-size TH9 - and draw the slide back about 1/8 inch. Pull the disassembly latch down with the other hand, release the slide, then release the latch.
steps.prose: That eighth of an inch lines the slide's takedown notch up with the latch and unloads it so it can rotate. Overshoot and the latch will not budge; the fix is to ease the slide forward slightly, never to force the latch. It should drop with almost no resistance when the slide is in the right place.
steps.quote: 2. Hold the pistol in the right or left hand in such a way that four fingers rest over the slide and thumb rests on the rear of the grip. Using the fingers draw back the slide about 1/8". With the other hand pull disassembly latch down. Release slide. Release disassembly latch.
steps.cite:
TH SERIES
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 7 — Disassembly, printed p.26 (PDF p.14)

steps.title: Pull and release the trigger, then take the slide off the front
steps.action: With the chamber already confirmed empty and the muzzle safe, pull the trigger and let it return, then run the slide forward off the frame.
steps.prose: On a TH9 the trigger press drops the hammer, and the hammer has to be down for the slide to clear. Do not try to shortcut this by decocking with the lever and skipping the press - the book's sequence is the press, and a decocked-but-not-pressed TH will still hang on the sear geometry as the slide comes forward.
steps.quote: 3. Pull and release trigger. Then remove the slide from
steps.cite:
TH SERIES
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 7 — Disassembly, printed p.26 (PDF p.14)

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly off the barrel
steps.action: Turn the slide over and lift the recoil spring assembly out of its seat on the underside of the barrel, keeping it under control as the tension releases.
steps.prose: The TH9's assembly is captive and stays assembled; the guide and spring are not separated for cleaning. It leaves the seat with a snap once the preload breaks, so cup a hand over it rather than pinching it out with fingertips.
steps.quote: 4. Release recoil spring assembly from its position on the bottom of the barrel.
steps.cite:
TH SERIES
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 7 — Disassembly, printed p.27 (PDF p.14)
steps.warn: Please take care to prevent the forcible ejection of the slide spring assembly plate and compressed slide spring assembly.

steps.title: Barrel out - forward, then up
steps.action: Push the barrel forward inside the slide until the locking lug clears the ejection port cut, then lift it up and out. That is frame, slide, barrel and recoil spring assembly.
steps.prose: Check the bore against a light with the barrel in hand. On a full-size 9mm the leade just ahead of the chamber is where carbon builds first, and it is easier to see now than through a slide.
steps.quote: 5. Remove the barrel from the slide by pulling it to the front and up.
steps.cite:
TH SERIES
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 7 — Disassembly, printed p.27 (PDF p.14)

steps.title: Light oil film, clear bore, dry crevices
steps.action: Keep the pistol clean and covered with a light film of good quality oil to prevent corrosion, and keep the bore free of debris. Wipe with a lightly oiled cloth, do the same through the bore, remove the excess and brush the dust out of the crevices with a small clean brush.
steps.prose: A hammer gun has one extra place worth the brush: the hammer channel at the rear of the frame, where carbon and lint collect around the hammer and its spring guide. It is reachable from outside with a brush and does not need any disassembly, and a gummed hammer channel shows up as a heavy double-action pull long before it shows up as a failure.
steps.quote: In order to keep a firearm safe to use, it must be kept clean and covered with a light film of good quality oil to prevent corrosion. The barrel bore should be cleaned and left free of debris.
steps.cite:
TH SERIES
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 7 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.31 (PDF p.16)

steps.title: Do not carry these steps to a look-alike
steps.action: Before reassembly, note Taurus's own scope warning: firearms that look nearly the same differ widely in the location and function of their controls. The TH9's latch takedown is not the GX4's screwdriver-turned takedown pin, and its decocker has no equivalent on the striker-fired Taurus pistols.
steps.prose: Inside the TH book itself there is a further trap worth naming: the parts list carries entries flagged for one version only - the barrel recoil spring exists ONLY on the T380 version, and the right-side slide catch and its screw only on the STD version. A parts diagram in a multi-model book is not a picture of your gun.
steps.aside: FIREARMS ARE NOT ALL ALIKE - Many makes and models of firearms might LOOK nearly the same. However, they differ widely in design, operation, and in the location and function of various controls.
steps.cite:
TH SERIES
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 7 — Part List, printed p.33 (PDF p.17)

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel and recoil spring assembly. Taurus stops the owner there and sends everything else to a skilled gunsmith, so the hammer, sear, firing pin block, extractor and trigger bar stay inside the gun.
steps.prose: Two owner procedures are published beyond the field strip and neither is part of a routine clean: the magazine strip, and the backstrap change on full-size models. Deep Clean walks both.
steps.quote: No further disassembly is recommended unless done by a skilled gunsmith.
steps.cite:
TH SERIES
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 7 — Backstrap Disassembly, printed p.28 (PDF p.15)

deepSteps.title: Magazine: punch the seat, floorplate forward
deepSteps.action: Press a punch onto the magazine spring seat through the hole in the floor plate and hold it, then slide the floor plate toward the FRONT of the magazine. Keep a thumb over the plate as it comes clear.
deepSteps.prose: A 17-round TH9 body has a long spring stacked hard, so the seat leaves with real energy - more than the compact bodies in the same book. Front is the direction; the retainer's dimple faces rearward in the slot and pushing the plate back only wedges it tighter.
deepSteps.quote:
A) Use a punch to press in on magazine spring seat/clip.
B) Slide the magazine floor plate toward the front of the magazine according Position 1 and 2.
deepSteps.cite:
TH SERIES
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 7 — Magazine Disassembly, printed p.28 (PDF p.15)
deepSteps.warn: Please take care to prevent the forcible ejection of the magazine spring plate and compressed magazine spring, and wear the ANSI Z87.1+ eye protection Taurus specifies.

deepSteps.title: Spring and follower out, then reassemble in reverse
deepSteps.action: Withdraw the spring plate and spring from the body, invert the magazine and remove the follower, then assemble in reverse order. Brush the body out dry and wipe the follower - no oil goes inside a magazine.
deepSteps.prose: Note which way both the spring's closed coil and the follower faced. A TH9 follower will go back inverted and still fit, and it will still feed fifteen of seventeen rounds before failing, which makes it one of the hardest self-inflicted faults to trace.
deepSteps.quote:
C) Withdraw magazine spring plate and magazine spring
1 from magazine body. Turn magazine upside down and remove
magazine follower.
D) Assemble in reverse order.
deepSteps.cite:
TH SERIES
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 7 — Magazine Disassembly, printed p.28 (PDF p.15)

deepSteps.title: Backstrap off - full-size TH9 only
deepSteps.action: With the magazine out and the pistol confirmed clear, drive the backstrap pin away from the grip with an appropriately sized punch, then pull the backstrap off toward the bottom. To refit, offer the backstrap up to the grip and insert the pin, using a tool to make it easier.
deepSteps.prose: There are three sizes and the point of the change is trigger reach, not cleaning - but taking the backstrap off is the only way to get properly at the grit that collects behind it on a carry gun. Choose the size by whether your finger lands centred on the trigger face, and check the pin is fully home afterwards; a proud backstrap pin drags on a holster and eventually walks out.
deepSteps.caution: Taurus lists the adjustable backstrap as a FULL SIZE models only feature. On a TH9C there is nothing here to remove, and this step does not apply.
deepSteps.quote: There are three backstrap sizes available, with easy replacement, according to the instructions below: A) REMOVAL: using an appropriate diameter punch, move the backstrap pin away from the grip. After that, remove the backstrap, pulling it towards the bottom.
deepSteps.cite:
TH SERIES
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 7 — Backstrap Disassembly, printed p.28 (PDF p.15)

cleaning.name: BORE, CHAMBER & FEED RAMP
tasks: Run a properly fitted brush wet with solvent through the bore from the chamber end, then a dry patch, and finish with a lightly oiled pass
Scrub the chamber and the leade - the ring just ahead of the chamber is where a full-size 9mm cokes first
Clean the feed ramp and the outside of the chamber hood
Hold the barrel up to a light and confirm a clear bore before it goes back in the slide

cleaning.name: SLIDE, BREECH FACE & EXTRACTOR
tasks: Wipe the slide inside and out with a lightly oiled cloth and take the excess off
Pick carbon off the breech face and out from behind the extractor claw
Check the loaded chamber indicator moves freely - it is a small part that fouling jams proud
Leave the firing pin block and firing pin alone; both are behind the slide cap and past what this book publishes

cleaning.name: FRAME, HAMMER CHANNEL & MAGAZINES
tasks: Brush dust and residue out of all crevices with a small clean brush, hammer channel included
Work the safety/decocker lever through its full travel on both sides of a full-size TH9 and confirm both sides move together
Oil the frame rails lightly and wipe the excess
Wipe magazine bodies externally and leave their interiors dry
A pistol with a laser must not be cleaned in a well or supersonic machine that submerges it

reassembly: Replace the barrel in the slide, pushing it to the rearward position.
Insert the recoil spring assembly into the slide over the barrel, compressing the spring slightly to get it into position.
Mount the slide on the frame, pull it fully to the rear and move the slide catch upward to hold the slide back, then release it.
Cycle the slide several times with no magazine inserted and an empty chamber to confirm the barrel / slide / frame relationship is correct.
fncheck: With the pistol confirmed empty: the slide should run fully and return into battery under spring pressure; the double-action pull should stage and break with the hammer following through, and the single-action pull should reset crisply as the slide returns; the decocker must drop the hammer without the trigger being touched, and on a full-size TH9 it must do so from BOTH sides; the safety must go fully up to 'on' with no middle position; and the slide catch should hold on an empty magazine. Taurus's warning applies to the lever as much as the gun - a safety lever between 'on' and 'off' is not a safety.
